//name: Scoped because unscoped `pi-workflows` is taken on npm by an unrelated package. The name is not cosmetic: it is the specifier every authored workflow imports, so it also appears in the loader's virtual-module map and in what /workflow create generates.
name: @pmateusz/pi-workflows
description: Define arbitrary workflows in TypeScript and run them inside the PI coding harness.
author: pmateusz
//files: `src` only, and deliberately as TypeScript: every `exports` target is a `.ts` file because PI loads extensions and workflows through jiti, so there is no build output to ship and the source doubles as the types. Tests, benchmarks and the spec stay out of the tarball.
//exports: The public surface, and the only names anything outside this repo may import. The package root IS the authoring API — that is what a workflow file imports; `./flow` names the same module for symmetry with the other layers. Directory paths (`./src/...`) are deliberately NOT exported: the layout is ours to change. Also what makes SELF-reference work: without an exports map, a workflow file inside this repo could not import the package by name at all.
//pi: The PI package manifest (docs/packages.md), which is what makes `pi install <path|git:…>` load the /workflow command. Without it PI records the package in settings and loads NOTHING from it — a package.json with no `pi` key and no conventional `extensions/` directory contributes no resources.
//dependencies: `jiti` only. PI does NOT provide it to extensions (verified: a package importing it with no node_modules fails to load), and workflow loading needs it at runtime.
//peerDependencies: The packages PI bundles and hands to extensions itself (docs/packages.md: "list them in peerDependencies with a \"*\" range and do not bundle them"). PI's extension loader aliases these specifiers to its own copies and that alias WINS over the consuming project's node_modules — so a range narrower than `*` would describe a resolution we do not control.
//devDependencies: `typebox` is pinned EXACTLY to the version `@earendil-works/pi-coding-agent` pins, because that is the copy the harness actually runs us on — a caret range let tests pass on 1.3.6 while every real run used PI's 1.1.38. `test/typebox-pin.test.ts` fails when a PI upgrade moves this.
